scenario.name: Splunk STRT & Mandiant — Ivanti Connect Secure (UNC5221): Auth Bypass, RCE & ZIPLINE Backdoor
scenario.shortSubtitle: Splunk STRT / Mandiant UNC5221 · CVE-2023-46805 + CVE-2024-21887, libdsupgrade.so ZIPLINE & CAV Tamper
scenario.overview: Imagine a grand city courthouse hall with fluted marble columns, an elevated wooden judge bench, a witness stand, and a brass wax-seal notary stamping desk. Entering the marble courthouse hall during a crowded docket, a forger requests a routine certified copy at the notary clerk’s brass stamping counter. In this real-world scenario, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass courthouse wax-seal press, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the court notary clerk's station. The court bailiff audits the official notary stamp registry and discovers stamped certificates that were never entered into the judge’s docket book. In this scenario (CVE-2024-21887, Splunk STRT & Mandiant, Ivanti Connect Secure (UNC5221): Auth Bypass, RCE & ZIPLINE Backdoor), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: bypassing Authentication With ../../, then injecting Shell Commands Into keys-status, then implanting "WIREFIRE" in visits.py. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Bypassing Authentication With ../../, then Injecting Shell Commands Into keys-status, then Implanting "WIREFIRE" in visits.py, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: PATH TRAVERSAL AUTH BYPASS & RCE (CVE-2023-46805 + CVE-2024-21887)
stages.subtitle: Chaining /api/v1/totp/user-backup-code/../../ with cloud-server-test-connection
stages.description: Entering the marble courthouse hall during a crowded docket, a forger requests a routine certified copy at the notary clerk’s brass stamping counter. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass courthouse wax-seal press while everyday visitors and the court notary clerk go about their routine. In Ivanti Connect Secure, the outer web gatekeeper checks whether a requested URL starts with a public prefix like /api/v1/totp/user-backup-code/ (an endpoint that must be reachable before login so users who lost their phone can submit a backup 2FA code). By requesting /api/v1/totp/user-backup-code/../../license/keys-status/, the outer gatekeeper sees the allowed prefix and waves the request through without asking for a password, while the internal Python router resolves the "../../" path traversal and hands the request straight to the restricted admin-only /api/v1/license/keys-status/ endpoint. Because the authentication filter checked the raw un-normalized URI prefix (startswith("/api/v1/totp/user-backup-code")) before the backend web framework normalized "../" segments (CVE-2023-46805), any unauthenticated internet client can reach any internal REST API endpoint on the VPN appliance. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ CVE-2024-21887 RCE / ⇠#1 ALERT HTTP 200) from Node ① (#1 UNC5221 / UTA0178 Actor) to Node ② (#2 DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Splunk Enterprise Security (STRT)).

stages.title: ZIPLINE ELF BACKDOOR IN LIBDSUPGRADE.SO & CAV TAMPERING
stages.subtitle: Replacing /home/lib/libdsupgrade.so and neutralizing the internal Integrity Checker
stages.description: Taking advantage of an unguarded moment at the notary desk, the forger lifts the impression of the courthouse wax seal and stamps a stack of unauthorized passes offline. Here in Step 2 inside the courthouse, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the brass courthouse wax-seal press without disturbing the sealed judicial record vault. Once the path-traversal request reaches /api/v1/license/keys-status/;python%20-c%20..., the backend Python handler takes the URL parameter and passes it directly into subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True) without input sanitization (CVE-2024-21887, an OS command injection flaw where untrusted URL characters are interpreted as live Linux shell commands). Inside that string, the semicolon (; which in Bash/sh terminates the legitimate license-check command and immediately executes the attacker’s python -c payload right behind it) runs the attacker’s code with full root privileges. Why did the attacker chain two CVEs? Because CVE-2024-21887 (command injection in keys-status) normally required an administrator login, and CVE-2023-46805 (path traversal) only bypassed authentication without running code. Combining both inside a single HTTP URL turns them into a 1-packet unauthenticated root RCE. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ ZIPLINE ELF HOOK / ⇠#2 ALERT 72 KB ELF) from Node ② (#2 DMZ Reverse Proxy & SPAN Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Ivanti Connect Secure VPN), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Splunk Enterprise Security (STRT)).

stages.title: DSLOG.PM CREDENTIAL HARVESTING & INTERNAL TUNNELING
stages.subtitle: Intercepting plaintext VPN logins and proxying into Active Directory
stages.description: Every forged document now bears the court’s own authentic wax emblem, letting the holder command authority in any neighboring municipal hall. In this final step inside the courthouse, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the court notary clerk's station until the court bailiff stamp registry catches the mismatch. Synthesizing Volexity (UTA0178) and Mandiant (UNC5221) findings, with root access on the VPN appliance the attacker runs mount -o remount,rw / (temporarily unlocking the appliance’s read-only system partition so built-in files can be edited) and deploys a multi-layered malware suite: (1) Volexity’s WIREFIRE Python webshell injected directly inside visits.py (modifying an already-existing API file so basic file-count checks do not spot an extra file) and WARPWIRE JavaScript credential harvester injected into the VPN login page to steal plaintext Active Directory passwords; plus (2) Mandiant’s ZIPLINE passive backdoor loaded via LD_PRELOAD inside libsecure.so (intercepting accept() network calls inside the legitimate Ivanti web daemon). As Mandiant UNC5221 documented, the threat actor also patches ComponentIntegrity.pm (so Ivanti’s built-in Integrity Checker Tool reports "0 modified files" when an admin runs an internal self-check, which is why CISA ED 24-01 mandated running the external offline ICT snapshot tool). Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ DSLOG.PM CRED STEAL / ⇠#3 ACK Cred Harvest) from Node ③ (#3 Ivanti Connect Secure VPN) to Node ④ (#4 ZIPLINE Passive Backdoor), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Splunk Enterprise Security (STRT)).

detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Ivanti Connect Secure Path Traversal and Command Injection
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:

      - '/api/v1/totp/user-backup-code/../../'

  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Apply Ivanti Connect Secure patches, run the external Integrity Checker Tool (ICT), and factory-reset any appliance showing signs of compromise.

detectionRule.title: Mandiant Official YARA — M_Hunting_Backdoor_ZIPLINE_1
detectionRule.ruleCode:
rule Mandiant_Backdoor_Linux_ZIPLINE {
  meta:
    author = "Mandiant"
    description = "Detects ZIPLINE passive ELF backdoor in libdsupgrade.so"
  strings:
    $magic = "I5033248" ascii
    $path1 = "/tmp/data/root/home/lib/libdsupgrade.so" ascii
    $path2 = "send_file_to_server" ascii
  condition:
    uint32(0) == 0x464C457F and ($magic or ($path1 and $path2))
}
detectionRule.mitigation: Use only the external, boot-time Integrity Checker Tool (ICT) rather than the internal web UI scanner (which UNC5221 patches via cav-0.1-py2.7.egg).
